title: In Vivo T1 Mapping of Blood-Brain Barrier Leakage in Mouse Brain Using MRI
author: Vladimir Grouza
materials: Body temperature and respiration should be monitored continuously.

steps.title: Record mouse body weight
steps.instruction: Weigh each mouse and record its body weight before any induction.

steps.title: Induce and maintain anesthesia
steps.instruction: Induce anesthesia with isoflurane and maintain it at 2–3% throughout MRI acquisition.

steps.title: Apply ocular protection
steps.instruction: Apply eye gel to both eyes to prevent corneal damage.

steps.title: Prepare tail‑vein catheter
steps.instruction: Clean the tail vein with 70 % ethanol, insert a catheter into the tail vein, and secure it to prevent blood loss.

steps.title: Inject contrast and saline
steps.instruction: Dilute the gadolinium‑based contrast agent (GBCA) in saline, then inject via the tail‑vein catheter at 0.4 mmol kg⁻¹; immediately inject 500 µL saline intraperitoneally to keep the mouse hydrated.

steps.title: Position mouse in scanner
steps.instruction: Place the mouse securely in the MRI bore, use the same geometry for all animals, ensure consistent slice placement, and maintain physiological stability throughout imaging.

steps.title: Acquire pre‑contrast dataset
steps.instruction: Acquire the full pre‑contrast RARE‑VTR dataset using the TR series 8000, 3600, 2400, 1480, 940, 650, and 501.1 ms with identical geometry for all mice.

steps.title: Perform immediate QC scan
steps.instruction: Immediately after GBCA injection, run a rapid QC scan (single RARE acquisition) and verify visible post‑contrast hyperintensity in soft tissue.

steps.title: Acquire post‑contrast dataset
steps.instruction: Repeat the full RARE‑VTR acquisition post‑contrast using the same geometry and TR values as the pre‑contrast scan; avoid any repositioning between scans.

steps.title: Reconstruct MRI data
steps.instruction: Reconstruct raw MRI data offline with the Bruker2Nifti reconstruction workflow.

steps.title: Correct motion artifacts
steps.instruction: For each RARE‑VTR 4D dataset, compute a rigid‑body transformation between the TR = 8000 ms volume and each other TR volume, then apply the transformation to align all volumes.

steps.title: Denoise and remove ringing
steps.instruction: Apply Marcenko‑Pastur PCA denoising and Gibbs‑ringing correction using DiPy v1.4.0.

steps.title: Bias‑field correction
steps.instruction: Perform N3 bias‑field correction (ANTs) on the brain‑masked TR = 8000 ms image and apply the estimated field to all other volumes.

steps.title: Register to anatomical atlas
steps.instruction: Register the corrected mouse brain image to a 40 × 40 × 40 µm anatomical template using affine registration with 12 degrees of freedom; invert the transform and project atlas labels back into native space with nearest‑neighbor interpolation for ROI parcellation.

steps.title: Segment brain tissue
steps.instruction: Segment the brain from skull and surrounding tissue using the SHERM algorithm in MATLAB (Version R2019b).

steps.title: Fit voxel‑wise T1 maps
steps.instruction: Fit a monoexponential saturation‑recovery model voxel‑wise with a nonlinear least‑squares solver in MATLAB to generate whole‑brain pre‑ and post‑contrast T1 maps for each specimen.

steps.title: Quantify regional T1 shift
steps.instruction: Within each ROI, create histograms of pre‑ and post‑contrast T1 values and compute the Earth Mover’s Distance between paired histograms to quantify contrast‑induced T1 shortening.

description: Figure 2. Overview of the image-processing workflow for T1 mapping and regional brain delineation. This figure presents the main steps of the image-processing pipeline used for T1 mapping and region-of-interest (ROI) analysis. The images are shown in three anatomical orientations: coronal (left), axial (middle), and sagittal (right). Panel (i) shows the TR = 8000 ms image after correction of imaging artefacts. Panel (ii) shows the brain mask generated using the SHERM-based segmentation method. Panel (iii) shows the atlas labels transformed back onto the native TR = 8000 ms image using the inverse affine transformation. Each color corresponds to a distinct anatomical ROI used for downstream segmentation and analysis.
